sara-support: Heads up — ACME reported a spike of 401s and ~300-500ms extra tail latency for EU users starting ~08:10 UTC. They say the requests appear to be served from us-east (auth token mismatch). :grimacing:
aj-ops: Do we have a recent DNS rollout or GeoIP DB update?
deploy-bot: (deploy) dns-prefetch-rollout v2 -> 100% completed at 2023-11-21T07:58:09Z
ka-te-sre (kate-sre): @sara-support can you paste the request headers + IP seen on server?
sara-support: customer-provided excerpt: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, `Host: api.redwood.ai`, `X-Forwarded-For: 54.92.10.77`
sara-support: they also ran `curl -I` and saw `x-region: us-east-1` in our edge response
mike-neteng: sounds like resolver prefetch/TTL jitter to me — some resolvers may be returning cached us-east answers for eu clients. Which resolver do they use? any EDU/ISP?
sara-support: customer says ISP is "NordConnect" in Poland; they showed `dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` returning a us-east LB IP.
mike-neteng: ask them to run `dig +trace @resolver <customer-ip>` and `dig +short api.redwood.ai @<their-resolver>` and paste. Also check EDNS client subnet (ECS) stripping.
aj-ops: quick check: our GeoIP DB rolled at 07:55 UTC and we pushed a prefetch TTL tweak in the edge config at 07:50. @mike-neteng could the prefetch logic cause transient overshoots? :eyes:
mike-neteng: yes, if prefetch jitter was widened the resolver priming could have bumped old us-east records into caches. Also some ISP resolvers ignore ECS and will keep stale CNAME answers for TTLs.
kate-sre: let's correlate with auth logs — if token audience/region checks fail because request hit us-east, that'll produce the 401 pattern. Sara, can you attach a minimal repro? (curl incl. Host and auth header replaced with token placeholder)
sara-support: repro sent to #incidents and attached to ticket 34721. Minimal repro: ```curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat' -H 'Host: api.redwood.ai' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST' -H 'Accept: application/json'```
kate-sre: thanks. mitigation options: 1) short-term - add region-pin header handling so we honor `X-Region-Hint` for auth routing; 2) force negative cache purge on edge for affected prefixes; 3) rollback the prefetch jitter change if we confirm correlation.
aj-ops: can we push a purge to major ISP resolvers? we can issue an emergency DNS change but risk propagation churn.
mike-neteng: prefer targeted purge + manual GeoIP DB check. I'll run a probe set from eu-pop nodes and report in 10m.
sara-support: customer accepted temporary `X-Region-Hint` and sees immediate drop in 401s. :thumbsup: They still worry about residual latency while caches expire.
dns-bot: (alert) GeoIP DB update detected 07:55 UTC, prefetched TTL window=120s -> candidates: eu-west-1, us-east-1
mike-neteng: confirmed — prefetched TTL jitter was +30-90s. I'm opening an infra ticket to tighten jitter and add a safelist for ECS-stripping ISPs.
kate-sre: action items: 1) mike -> tighten prefetch jitter + probe results (ETA 30m); 2) infra -> consider rollback if probes show more than 5% misroute; 3) support -> notify customer with repro notes and ETA.
sara-support: sending status update to ACME now (ticket 34721). I'll attach repro commands and note the temporary `X-Region-Hint` workaround.
aj-ops: leaving notes in runbook: add step to check `dig +short` from multiple public resolvers and confirm `x-region` header on initial request.
mike-neteng: probe results: 6/12 eu probes saw us-east answers; majority were resolvers with known ECS stripping. Will follow up with per-ISP list.
kate-sre: good find. once jitter is tightened and we purge, monitor auth error rate for 1 hour before closing.
sara-support: closing loop with customer, they marked as "mitigated" for now, will reopen if it recurs. Thanks team. :heart:
